messages:
kyla: Quick heads-up — CI similarity-eval job is flaking hard. Recall@10 jumps between runs: 0.78 -> 0.62 on the same commit. Reproduced twice in CI, can't repro consistently locally yet. :eyes:

ci-bot: CI build #542 — tests/similarity/test_recall.py::test_recall_stability failed (flakiness above threshold). Full logs: <https://ci.redwood/542/logs>

tariq: I glanced at the logs. Two immediate suspects: non-deterministic FAISS index build + multi-threaded BLAS/Omp variations in the container. We've seen tiny RNG/ordering differences hurt recall numbers on small test sets.

alex: Which dataset/split? small-collections or the mteb-mini we added last week? Also did the job use quantized vectors or float32?

kyla: It's the mteb-mini subset, float32 vectors, no quantization. Here's the failing excerpt from the CI log:

```
--- FAIL: TestRecallStability (0.23s)
expected recall@10 >= 0.75, got 0.62
run seeds: [42]
faiss build params: nlist=128, nprobe=8
ENV: OMP_NUM_THREADS=8, MKL_NUM_THREADS=8
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/similarity/test_recall.py", line 87, in test_recall_stability
    assert recall >= 0.75
```

kyla: Note the job runs with single seed in CI (default harness). Locally I got 0.77 on one run and 0.63 on another when I didn't pin OMP threads.

tariq: Ok actionable plan: 1) make the eval runner pass a deterministic seed to FAISS index construction and all RNGs (numpy, random, torch if used); 2) set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 in CI job to reduce BLAS nondeterminism; 3) add a stability collector that runs the test with 3 distinct seeds and fails the job only if mean +/- std crosses threshold.

alex: +1. Also add a deterministic build flag for FAISS if available. There is a known option to force single-threaded index build or to use a deterministic ordering when constructing IVF centers. I'll add a small helper in the harness (eval/runner/index_utils.py) to wrap index builds with a seed.

kyla: I'll open a small PR that: pins seeds (numpy/random), sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 in the job matrix, and changes the CI test to run seeds [42, 1337, 2026] and publish mean+std to the metrics pipeline. Will also add a short note in the dashboard mapping so the MTEB panel shows CI stability instead of just raw recall.

alex: For the dashboard: add a new series `recall10_mean` and `recall10_std` and a red alert if mean - 2*std < threshold. That should catch regressions caused by noise.

ci-bot: Noted: created ticket INF-1284 to add multi-seed stability collector and env pinning.

kyla: Thanks — will link PR here when ready. If anyone sees other nondeterministic bits (disk race during index write) flag them. :thumbsup:

alex: One more thought — if quantization experiments start later, we should run the same stability matrix but include quantized variants as separate series so we can compare noise profiles.

kyla: Yep. I'll include a TODO in the PR for quantized runs.

ci-bot: Build #543 queued with env fixes (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1). Will run the 3-seed stability job after PR merge.
